what_happened: On a freeway with a RIGHT command, the ego kept its planned path straight and slightly left instead of following the recorded path to the right. It drifted across the left yellow edge line onto the median shoulder at about 9 m/s and went offroad at 12.0 s, about 5 m from the human trajectory. The camera view was clean at 10 s; the smears at 11–12 s appeared only after the ego had already moved off the recording.

On a multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT command, the policy planned a lane change to the left, first toward actor 15 and then toward actor 37. It sped up from 4.2 to 5.8 m/s and steered left into actor 56, which was driving alongside it in the adjacent lane, causing a front collision at 6.7 s. The rear contact recorded in this run came after this at-fault collision.

On a multi-lane freeway with a STRAIGHT command, the ego took over at 4.6s, then steered left out of its lane at about 8 m/s toward the adjacent lane. Its front-left hit vehicle 33, which was travelling alongside it in that lane. The camera view looked clean before the impact, so nothing in the rendering explains this unprompted lane change. Vehicle 33 was already alongside when the ego cut over.

After handoff, the policy steered left out of its lane when the command was STRAIGHT (later RIGHT) and the recorded path stayed in lane. It sped up from 4.2 to 5.9 m/s and its front hit vehicle 56, which was driving alongside it in the adjacent left lane. The rear contact recorded at the same time was secondary to this front collision.

On a multi-lane highway, the ego was going straight in its lane and speeding up from 4.2 to 5.8 m/s, which put it ahead of where the human drove. Actor 56, which had been beside it in the left lane, cut over into the ego's path. The ego's front then hit 56 (the gap ahead fell from 21.5 m to 3.2 m) before the policy reacted.

On a multi-lane freeway at about 8 m/s, the policy took over at 4.6 s. By 5.2 s its predicted path (orange) bent left toward the next lane. The ego drifted about 0.9 m left of the recorded human path, and at 6.2 s its front-left corner hit actor 33, which was passing in the adjacent left lane. Nothing was blocking it ahead (the lead car was about 25 m away). The camera smear at 6.2 s happens at the impact itself, so it doesn't explain the drift.

The ego was cruising straight in its lane at about 8 m/s with a 25 m gap to the car ahead. Actor 33, a replayed vehicle, came up from behind on the left (it shows as 23 at 5.2s) and ran into the ego's left side and rear at 6.2s. The ego was only 0.9 m off the recorded path. The contact is flagged as a front collision, probably because the boxes overlap at the ego's front-left corner, but the ego wasn't closing on anything ahead, and the run also records a rear impact.

At 3.7s, while the ego was still replaying the logged path (0.0 m off it), actor 16 was right on its rear bumper. By 4.7s, the handoff moment, actor 16 had driven through the ego and was overlapping its front, so a front collision was recorded at the instant the policy took over. The policy never controlled the car before contact, so this is a replay-actor overlap rather than a driving error.

The ego was still replaying the recorded trajectory at about 14 m/s (0.0 m off the log) when actor 16 came up from directly behind in the same lane, overtook through the ego's footprint, and ended up overlapping its front. That overlap was scored as a front collision at 4.7 s, the same instant the policy took over, so the policy had no time to act.

The ego was going straight at about 14 m/s on the recorded path. Actor 16 came up from directly behind it at 3.7s, passed it on the right, and by 4.7s was overlapping the ego's front (the camera shows the car cutting in close on the right), which registered as a front collision. That was the exact moment the policy took over at handoff, so the policy had no chance to react; this looks like a replayed actor's path going through the ego, not a policy decision.

The ego was going straight at about 14 m/s, exactly on the recorded human path (0.0 m off). The collision is flagged at 4.7 s, the same moment as the handoff, so the policy had no time to react; this looks like replayed actor motion clashing with the logged ego path, not a policy mistake.

The rear contact the run also reports came after this front collision.
